pages.caption: Once upon a time, long, long ago, there were two brothers, the one rich and the other poor.
pages.scene: A poor brother begging

pages.caption: When Christmas Eve came, the poor one had not a bite in the house, either of meat or bread.
pages.scene: The poor brother on Christmas Eve

pages.caption: So he went to his brother, and begged him, in God's name, to give him something for Christmas Day.
pages.scene: The poor brother approaching his brother

pages.caption: "If you will do what I ask you, you shall have a whole ham," said he.
pages.scene: The rich brother with a ham

pages.caption: The poor one immediately thanked him, and promised this.
pages.scene: The poor brother receiving the ham

pages.caption: "Well, here is the ham, and now you must go straight to Dead Man's Hall," said the rich brother.
pages.scene: The rich brother throwing the ham

pages.caption: "Well, I will do what I have promised," said the other, and he took the ham and set off.
pages.scene: The poor brother setting off

pages.caption: He went on and on for the livelong day, and at nightfall he came to a place where there was a bright light.
pages.scene: The poor brother walking all day

pages.caption: "I have no doubt this is the place," thought the man with the ham.
pages.description: [The poor brother arriving at a place]
pages.scene: The poor brother arriving at a place

pages.caption: An old man with a long white beard was standing in the outhouse, chopping Yule logs.
pages.scene: An old man chopping Yule logs

pages.caption: "Good-evening," said the man with the ham.
pages.scene: A greeting at the outhouse

pages.caption: "Good-evening to you. Where are you going at this late hour?" said the man.
pages.description: [The old man asking the poor brother's business]
pages.scene: The old man asking the poor brother's business

pages.caption: "I am going to Dead Man's Hall, if only I am on the right track," answered the poor man.
pages.scene: The poor brother explaining his journey

pages.caption: "Oh! yes, you are right enough, for it is here," said the old man.
pages.scene: The old man giving advice

pages.caption: "When you get inside they will all want to buy your ham, for they don't get much meat to eat there."
pages.description: [The old man warning the poor brother about the mill]
pages.scene: The old man warning the poor brother about the mill

pages.caption: "But you must not sell it unless you can get the hand-mill which stands behind the door for it."
pages.description: [The old man telling about the hand-mill]
pages.scene: The old man telling about the hand-mill

pages.caption: "When you come out again I will teach you how to stop the hand-mill, which is useful for almost everything."
pages.description: [The old man teaching how to stop the mill]
pages.scene: The old man teaching how to stop the mill

pages.caption: So the man with the ham thanked the other for his good advice, and rapped at the door.
pages.description: [The poor brother thanking the old man]
pages.scene: The poor brother thanking the old man

pages.caption: When he got in, everything happened just as the old man had said it would.
pages.description: [The crowd gathering around the poor man]
pages.scene: The crowd gathering around the poor man

pages.caption: All the people, great and small, came round him like ants on an ant-hill, and each tried to outbid the other for the ham.
pages.scene: People trying to buy the ham

pages.caption: "By rights my old woman and I ought to have it for our Christmas dinner, but, since you have set your hearts upon it, I must just give it up to you," said the man.
pages.scene: The poor brother offering the ham

pages.caption: "But, if I sell it, I will have the hand-mill which is standing there behind the door."
pages.scene: The poor brother demanding the hand-mill

pages.caption: At first they would not hear of this, and haggled and bargained with the man, but he stuck to what he had said.
pages.description: [The people reluctantly giving up the mill]
pages.scene: The people reluctantly giving up the mill

pages.caption: The people were forced to give him the hand-mill.
pages.scene: The poor brother receiving the hand-mill

pages.caption: When the man came out again into the yard, he asked the old wood-cutter how he was to stop the hand-mill.
pages.description: [The poor brother asking the old man how to stop the mill]
pages.scene: The poor brother asking the old man how to stop the mill

pages.caption: And when he had learned that, he thanked him and set off home with all the speed he could.
pages.description: [The poor brother learning to stop the mill]
pages.scene: The poor brother learning to stop the mill

pages.caption: But he did not get there until after the clock had struck twelve on Christmas Eve.
pages.scene: The poor brother arriving home late

pages.caption: "Where in the world have you been?" said the old woman.
pages.scene: The old woman waiting at home

pages.caption: "Here I have sat waiting hour after hour, and have not even two sticks to lay across each other under the Christmas porridge-pot."
pages.scene: The old woman complaining

pages.caption: "Oh! I could not come before; I had something of importance to see about, and a long way to go, too; but now you shall just see!" said the man.
pages.scene: The poor brother showing the hand-mill

pages.caption: And then he set the hand-mill on the table, and bade it first grind light, then a table-cloth.
pages.description: [The man setting the hand-mill on the table]
pages.scene: The man setting the hand-mill on the table

pages.caption: And then meat, and beer, and everything else that was good for a Christmas Eve's supper; and the mill ground all that he ordered.
pages.scene: The mill grinding meat and beer

pages.caption: "Bless me!" said the old woman as one thing after another appeared.
pages.scene: The old woman amazed

pages.caption: And she wanted to know where her husband had got the mill from, but he would not tell her that.
pages.description: [The old woman asking where the mill came from]
pages.scene: The old woman asking where the mill came from

pages.caption: "Never mind where I got it; you can see that it is a good one, and the water that turns it will never freeze," said the man.
pages.description: [The man keeping the mill a secret]
pages.scene: The man keeping the mill a secret

pages.caption: So he ground meat and drink, and all kinds of good things, to last all Christmas-tide.
pages.scene: The man grinding food for Christmas

pages.caption: And on the third day he invited all his friends to come to a feast.
pages.description: [The man inviting friends to a feast]
pages.scene: The man inviting friends to a feast

pages.caption: Now when the rich brother saw all that there was at the banquet and in the house, he was both vexed and angry.
pages.scene: The rich brother seeing the feast

pages.caption: For he grudged everything his brother had.
pages.scene: The rich brother's jealousy

pages.caption: "On Christmas Eve he was so poor that he came to me and begged for a trifle, for God's sake, and now he gives a feast as if he were both a count and a king!" thought he.
pages.description: [The rich brother thinking of his brother's poverty]
pages.scene: The rich brother thinking of his brother's poverty

pages.caption: "But, for heaven's sake, tell me where you got your riches from," said he to his brother.
pages.scene: The rich brother demanding to know

pages.caption: "From behind the door," said he who owned the mill, for he did not choose to satisfy his brother on that point.
pages.scene: The poor brother's evasive answer

pages.caption: But later in the evening, when he had taken a drop too much, he could not refrain from telling how he had come by the hand-mill.
pages.scene: The poor brother revealing the secret

pages.caption: "There you see what has brought me all my wealth!" said he, and brought out the mill, and made it grind first one thing and then another.
pages.description: [The poor brother showing off the mill]
pages.scene: The poor brother showing off the mill

pages.caption: When the brother saw that, he insisted on having the mill, and after a great deal of persuasion got it.
pages.description: [The rich brother insisting on having the mill]
pages.scene: The rich brother insisting on having the mill

pages.caption: But he had to give three hundred dollars for it.
pages.description: [The rich brother paying for the mill]
pages.scene: The rich brother paying for the mill

pages.caption: And the poor brother was to keep it till the haymaking was over.
pages.description: [The poor brother keeping the mill temporarily]
pages.scene: The poor brother keeping the mill temporarily

pages.caption: For he thought: "If I keep it as long as that, I can make it grind meat and drink that will last many a long year."
pages.scene: The poor brother's plan

pages.caption: And when hay-harvest came the rich brother got it, but the other had taken good care not to teach him how to stop it.
pages.scene: The hay harvest arriving

pages.caption: It was evening when the rich man got the mill home, and in the morning he bade the old woman go out and spread the hay after the mowers.
pages.description: [The rich brother getting the mill home]
pages.scene: The rich brother getting the mill home

pages.caption: So, when dinner-time drew near, he set the mill on the kitchen-table, and said: "Grind herrings and milk pottage, and do it both quickly and well."
pages.description: [The rich brother setting the mill to work]
pages.scene: The rich brother setting the mill to work

pages.caption: So the mill began to grind herrings and milk pottage, and first all the dishes and tubs were filled.
pages.scene: The mill beginning to grind

pages.caption: And then it came out all over the kitchen-floor.
pages.scene: The pottage flooding the kitchen

pages.caption: The man twisted and turned it, and did all he could to make the mill stop.
pages.description: [The man trying to stop the mill]
pages.scene: The man trying to stop the mill

pages.caption: But, howsoever he turned it and screwed it, the mill went on grinding.
pages.scene: The mill grinding uncontrollably

pages.caption: And in a short time the pottage rose so high that the man was like to be drowned.
pages.scene: The pottage rising dangerously

pages.caption: So he threw open the parlor door, but it was not long before the mill had ground the parlor full too.
pages.scene: The man opening the parlor door

pages.caption: And it was with difficulty and danger that the man could go through the stream of pottage and get hold of the door-latch.
pages.scene: The man fleeing through the pottage

pages.caption: When he got the door open, he did not stay long in the room, but ran out.
pages.scene: The man running outside

pages.caption: And the herrings and pottage came after him, and it streamed out over both farm and field.
pages.scene: The pottage streaming outside

pages.caption: Now the old woman, who was out spreading the hay, began to think dinner was long in coming.
pages.description: [The old woman coming home from the hayfield]
pages.scene: The old woman coming home from the hayfield

pages.caption: And said to the women and the mowers: "Though the master does not call us home, we may as well go."
pages.description: [The old woman suggesting they go home]
pages.scene: The old woman suggesting they go home

pages.caption: So they began to straggle homeward, but when they had got a little way up the hill.
pages.scene: The workers heading home

pages.caption: They met the herrings and pottage and bread, all pouring forth and winding about one over the other.
pages.description: [The workers meeting the flood of food]
pages.scene: The workers meeting the flood of food

pages.caption: And the man himself in front of the flood.
pages.scene: The man fleeing before the flood

pages.caption: "Would to heaven that each of you had a hundred stomachs! Take care that you are not drowned in the pottage!" he cried.
pages.scene: The man warning the workers

pages.caption: As he went by them as if Mischief were at his heels, down to where his brother dwelt.
pages.scene: The man running to his brother

pages.caption: Then he begged him, for God's sake, to take the mill back again, and that in an instant.
pages.scene: The man begging for help

pages.caption: For, said he: "If it grind one hour more the whole district will be destroyed by herrings and pottage."
pages.scene: The man's warning

pages.caption: But the brother would not take it until the other paid him three hundred dollars, and that he was obliged to do.
pages.scene: The poor brother demanding payment

pages.caption: Now the poor brother had both the money and the mill again.
pages.description: [The poor brother with money and mill]
pages.scene: The poor brother with money and mill

pages.caption: So it was not long before he had a farmhouse much finer than that in which his brother lived.
pages.description: [The poor brother building a fine house]
pages.scene: The poor brother building a fine house

pages.caption: But the mill ground him so much money that he covered it with plates of gold.
pages.description: [The mill covering the house with gold]
pages.scene: The mill covering the house with gold

pages.caption: And the farmhouse lay close by the sea-shore, so it shone and glittered far out to sea.
pages.scene: The golden farmhouse by the sea

pages.caption: Everyone who sailed by there now had to be put in to visit the rich man in the gold farmhouse.
pages.scene: Sailors visiting the rich man

pages.caption: And everyone wanted to see the wonderful mill, for the report of it spread far and wide.
pages.scene: People wanting to see the mill

pages.caption: After a long, long time came also a skipper who wished to see the mill.
pages.scene: A skipper arriving

pages.caption: He asked if it could make salt. "Yes, it could make salt," said he who owned it.
pages.scene: The skipper asking about salt

pages.caption: And when the skipper heard that, he wished with all his might and main to have the mill, let it cost what it might.
pages.scene: The skipper desiring the mill

pages.caption: For, he thought, if he had it, he would get off having to sail far away over the perilous sea for freights of salt.
pages.scene: The skipper's thoughts

pages.caption: At first the man would not hear of parting with it, but the skipper begged and prayed.
pages.scene: The rich man refusing to sell

pages.caption: And at last the man sold it to him, and got many, many thousand dollars for it.
pages.scene: The skipper buying the mill

pages.caption: When the skipper had got the mill on his back he did not stay there long, for he was so afraid that the man would change his mind.
pages.scene: The skipper fleeing with the mill

pages.caption: And he had no time to ask how he was to stop it grinding, but got on board his ship as fast as he could.
pages.description: [The skipper not learning how to stop it]
pages.scene: The skipper not learning how to stop it

pages.caption: When he had gone a little way out to sea he took the mill on deck. "Grind salt, and grind both quickly and well," said the skipper.
pages.description: [The skipper setting the mill to work at sea]
pages.scene: The skipper setting the mill to work at sea

pages.caption: So the mill began to grind salt, till it spouted out like water.
pages.scene: The mill grinding salt

pages.caption: And when the skipper had got the ship filled he wanted to stop the mill.
pages.scene: The ship filling with salt

pages.caption: But whichsoever way he turned it, and how much soever he tried, it went on grinding.
pages.description: [The skipper unable to stop the mill]
pages.scene: The skipper unable to stop the mill

pages.caption: And the heap of salt grew higher and higher, until at last the ship sank.
pages.scene: The heap of salt growing higher

pages.caption: There lies the mill at the bottom of the sea, and still, day by day, it grinds on.
pages.description: [The mill at the bottom of the sea]
pages.scene: The mill at the bottom of the sea

pages.caption: And that is why the sea is salt.
pages.scene: The sea becoming salty
